elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The exception permits an assignment by Client to an affiliate without approval.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly covers a Client successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly covers a Client successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly covers a Client successor in a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink remains subject to Client's prior written approval for every assignment or transfer.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The mutual prior-approval requirement is expressly qualified by “not to be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that TrueLink shall never assign or transfer its rights to a competitor of Client.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a transaction successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice duty applies to Client's consent-free successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free successor exception applies only to Client; TrueLink still requires Client's prior written approval.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: There is no written-notice mechanism for a TrueLink successor assignment; prior written approval is required instead.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to successors require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign to an affiliate without TrueLink's consent, even though an affiliate need not be a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments other than assignments to successors.
elements.evidence: For Client assignments that remain subject to approval, TrueLink's approval is expressly not to be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink has no consent-free exception, so its assignments require Client's prior written approval.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors.
elements.evidence: Although the general approval standard is reasonableness, assignments to Client competitors are categorically prohibited and cannot proceed even with reasonably required consent, so the fallback consent regime does not cover all other assignments.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position. It does not satisfy the fallback because successor-assignment rights are not mutual, neither party has the required written-notice mechanism, Client affiliates remain consent-free, and TrueLink's competitor assignments are absolutely barred rather than governed solely by a consent standard. The redline is not minimal because “not to be unreasonably withheld” applies mutually, also limiting TrueLink's discretion over Client assignments outside the stated exceptions, whereas the preferred position requires that standard only for Client's consent to TrueLink assignments. The clause otherwise preserves the assignment framework and introduces no material contradiction.
